title_en: Guiding Case No. 245: Yang v. Intermediate People's Court of Xuzhou, Jiangsu Province — compensation for erroneous enforcement
ruling_gist_en: Where a people's court takes enforcement measures against stocks and other property of an enforcement respondent based on the equity registration, and the actual right holders, such as dormant shareholders, apply for state compensation based on a judgment confirming rights obtained after the people's court took enforcement measures and after the enforcement was completed, the people's court shall not support such application in accordance with the law.

full_text_en:
Guiding Case No. 245

Yang v. Xu Zhou Intermediate People’s Court of Jiangsu Province — dispute over compensation for erroneous enforcement

(Discussed and adopted by the Judicial Committee of the Supreme People’s Court, published on December 23, 2024)

**Keywords**  
State compensation; compensation for erroneous enforcement; right appearance; judgment confirming ownership  

**Ruling Gist**  
Where a people’s court takes enforcement measures against property such as stocks registered in the name of the person subject to enforcement based on equity registration, and the actual right holder, such as a dormant shareholder, applies for state compensation based on a judgment confirming ownership that was obtained after the people’s court took enforcement measures and completed enforcement, the people’s court shall not support such application in accordance with law.  

**Basic Facts**  
In January 2014, the Xuzhou Intermediate People’s Court of Jiangsu Province (hereinafter “Xuzhou Intermediate Court”) accepted the enforcement applications of several judgment creditors. During the enforcement process, based on a sequestrator’s attachment, the court took enforcement measures against the stocks involved, which were registered in the name of the person subject to enforcement, Jiangsu Mouli Investment Development Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter “Jiangsu Mouli Company”), and completed the enforcement in September 2014.  

On December 11, 2014, the Economic Development Zone People’s Court of Xuzhou, Jiangsu Province rendered a civil judgment (No. (2013) Kaishengchuzi No. 353), confirming that 1,976,000-odd shares of the stocks involved held by Jiangsu Mouli Company belonged to Yang. Yang, on the ground that the effective judgment had confirmed his ownership and that the enforcement acts of the Xuzhou Intermediate Court were erroneous, applied to the Xuzhou Intermediate Court for compensation. By decision (No. (2016) Su 03 Fa Pei No. 1) on June 19, 2017, the Xuzhou Intermediate Court rejected Yang’s state compensation application. Yang refused to accept this decision and applied to the Compensation Committee of the Jiangsu High People’s Court for a compensation decision.  

**Judgment**  
By state compensation decision (No. (2017) Su Wei Pei No. 10) on November 15, 2017, the Compensation Committee of the Jiangsu High People’s Court affirmed the decision of the Xuzhou Intermediate Court (No. (2016) Su 03 Fa Pei No. 1). Yang refused to accept this decision and petitioned to the Compensation Committee of the Supreme People’s Court. By decision (No. (2019) Zui Gao Fa Wei Pei Jian No. 95) on September 29, 2019, the Compensation Committee of the Supreme People’s Court rejected Yang’s petition.  

**Reasoning**  
The focus of the dispute in this case is: whether the preservation and enforcement measures taken by the Xuzhou Intermediate People’s Court of Jiangsu Province constituted erroneous enforcement and whether they infringed Yang’s property rights.  

First, a people’s court’s taking of enforcement measures against property such as stocks registered in the name of the person subject to enforcement based on equity registration does not constitute erroneous enforcement. Article 244 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People’s Republic of China (amended in 2012) provides: “If the person subject to enforcement fails to perform the obligations determined by the legal instrument in accordance with the enforcement notice, the people’s court has the authority to seal up, detain, freeze, auction, or sell off the portion of the property of the person subject to enforcement that should be used to perform the obligations...” Article 25 of the Provisions of the Supreme People’s Court on Several Issues Concerning the Handling of Objections to Enforcement and Reconsideration Cases by People’s Courts (Fa Shi [2015] No. 10) provides: “For objections raised by persons other than the parties involved, the people’s court shall judge whether such persons are right holders according to the following standards: ... (4) With respect to equities, the judgment shall be made based on the information registered with the administrative authority for industry and commerce and disclosed on the enterprise credit information publicity system...” According to the above provisions, since the stocks involved were registered in the name of the person subject to enforcement, Jiangsu Mouli Company, the Xuzhou Intermediate Court took preservation and enforcement measures based on the right appearance of equity registration, which did not violate the provisions of law. Because the person subject to enforcement, Jiangsu Mouli Company, failed to perform the obligations determined by the effective legal instrument in accordance with the enforcement notice, the Xuzhou Intermediate Court took enforcement measures against the sealed-up stocks, and the enforcement act was legally based.  

Second, Yang and Jiangsu Mouli Company entered into an equity nominee holding contract. This equity nominee holding contract is only binding on the two contracting parties and has the effect of public summons and public trust for third parties outside the contract. That is, the contract’s effect does not extend to third parties. The lawsuit for confirmation of equity filed by Yang confirmed that 1,976,000-odd shares of the stocks involved held by Jiangsu Mouli Company belonged to him. Since it could not be enforced later, Yang could claim rights from Jiangsu Mouli Company through civil proceedings to seek relief. However, his claim that the enforcement acts of the Xuzhou Intermediate Court were erroneous on the ground that they infringed his ownership right had no legal basis.  

Third, the Xuzhou Intermediate Court’s preservation of the stocks involved occurred before the preservation in Yang’s confirmation-of-rights case, and the sale of the stocks involved was completed before September 2014. Yang obtained the civil judgment (No. (2013) Kaishengchuzi No. 353) in December 2014, that is, after the Xuzhou Intermediate Court had completed the enforcement of selling off the stocks. Yang cannot use the civil judgment (No. (2013) Kaishengchuzi No. 353) obtained after the Xuzhou Intermediate Court had frozen and sold off the stocks to oppose the court’s enforcement measures, nor can he use it as a basis for claiming state compensation rights.  

In summary, the preservation and enforcement measures taken by the Xuzhou Intermediate People’s Court of Jiangsu Province did not constitute erroneous enforcement and did not infringe Yang’s property rights. Therefore, compensation should not be granted in accordance with law.  

**Relevant Legal Provisions**  
Article 255 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People’s Republic of China (Article 244 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People’s Republic of China as amended in 2012 is applicable to this case)  

Article 25 of the Provisions of the Supreme People’s Court on Several Issues Concerning the Handling of Objections to Enforcement and Reconsideration Cases by People’s Courts (Fa Shi [2015] No. 10, as amended in 2020)
